title: Rejecting round suffix
statement: Let $M_V,M_I,M_P$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, and let $x,u,v$ be Boolean words such that the fixed-width increment of $u$ is $v$ and $|v|=|u|$. Start the associated round-body machine in its clearing phase with its first work tape storing $u$, its second storing $x$ followed by $u$, all other tapes blank, input-head position $1$, and the specified initial work-head positions at zero. There is a positive time $T$ at which it reaches the test-anchor configuration with first tape storing $v$, all other tapes blank, input-head position $1$, and the specified work-head positions zero; at every earlier time it is neither in the test-anchor state nor in the test phase's true-verdict state. At every time through $T$, every work-tape head position has absolute value at most $|x|+|u|+1$.
hypotheses_covered: $M_V,M_I,M_P$ are finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet
caveat: The exact phase-state and tape roles come from specialized machine constructions; the statement summarizes the specified configurations and bounds.
